title: Property-based differential testing: generate chains, compare oracles
description:
## Why

Unbounded supply of inputs, and it finds shapes no human corpus author thought of. Complements the fixed corpora rather than replacing them: PKITS and x509-limbo are finite and now largely agreed-on, so their marginal yield is near zero, while a generator keeps producing novel topologies.

## What

Generate certificate chains with a shrinking generator (proptest or quickcheck) over the dimensions that actually change verdicts:

* chain length, self-issued certificates interleaved, cross-signed alternatives
* name constraints: form, permitted vs excluded, nesting depth, empty subtree sets
* basicConstraints pathLenConstraint vs real depth
* validity windows straddling the evaluation time, inclusive bounds
* policy OIDs, mappings, inhibit/require counters
* extension criticality and duplication

Then compare pkix-path against openssl and pyca through the existing pkix-difftest oracle interface, and shrink any disagreement to a minimal chain.

## Why this is worth more than it sounds

Every generated chain needs a valid signature, so the generator has to sign as it builds -- which means it doubles as a fixture factory. Several tests this session needed a fixture no generator could produce (an OID-valued commonName, a duplicated extension, a non-conformant GeneralSubtree) and each was hand-rolled DER. A chain generator with signing would have produced all three.

## Relationship to PKIX-hbzo.3

That bead says the corpus gates pin disagreement as expected and so cannot detect being wrong. A generator has the same hazard in reverse: it has no ground truth, only oracle agreement. Majority vote is not truth -- all three oracles can be wrong together, and on the BetterTLS nameConstraints family two of them are. Record disagreements for classification; do not auto-accept agreement as correctness.
